card.name: Dosing instruction openers before regimen details
card.fires_on: Small words and verbs in dosing instructions that come right before a diet, meal or dose amount, such as 'to' after 'adjunct', 'Take' before 'orally with meals', or the empty spot just before a dose number.

modes.label: Adjunct to diet
modes.description: The word 'to' or 'a' after 'adjunct' leading into a reduced-calorie diet.
modes.example: Select patients for SAXENDA treatment as an adjunct<< to>> a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical

modes.label: Instruction verb
modes.description: Verbs like Take, taking or Using that start a how-to-take or patient-group instruction.
modes.example: •<< Take>> orally with meals to reduce gastrointestinal adverse reactions

modes.label: Before a dose number
modes.description: The position just before a dose amount in mg, after a phrase like 'start' or 'is'.
modes.example: The recommended dosage of rivastigmine tartrate capsules in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is<< >>6 mg to 12 mg per
